title: Intake & Escalation Flow for Data Controls: Audit Exports, PII Requests, and Retention Exceptions
creator: Riley Nguyen
description: Create a pragmatic intake and escalation playbook that productizes decision-making for non-bug customer requests that touch logging redaction, retention extensions, PII handling, and audit export needs. The goal is to: 1) reduce ambiguity for frontline support and AMs, 2) set clear SLAs and routing rules by risk tier, 3) provide deterministic approvals and escalation paths to Legal, Security, and Engineering, and 4) surface auditability for enterprise compliance reviews.
acceptance_criteria: A single intake form/template exists and is published for CS/AMs with required fields for risk assessment
SLA matrix covering Triage/Approval/Delivery times published and validated with Support/AMs
Routing rules implemented as a documented decision checklist mapping requests to teams: CS -> Solutions Eng -> Legal/Security -> Eng
Two sample real-customer requests simulated end-to-end and documented (including audit trail)
Stakeholder contact list and escalation contact tree published in Confluence
Security review sign-off template added and linked to intake flow
decision_checklist: Does the request include a specific customer identifier and use-case summary? (yes => continue; no => request clarification)
Does the request require access to raw logs or PII? (yes => mark as HIGH risk)
Is retention modification temporary (time-limited) or permanent? (temporary => preferred; permanent => escalate)
Can the requirement be satisfied by providing pre-filtered exports or summarized aggregates? (yes => propose lower-risk alternative)
Does the request require schema-level redaction/transform vs. ad-hoc export? (schema changes => Eng + SRE review)
Is there a regulatory/legal driver (e.g., audit, subpoena, contractual clause)? (yes => Legal early involvement)
Are there export encryption / KMS constraints or cross-region transfer concerns? (yes => Security + Infra)
Customer SLA expectations vs. Redwood standard SLAs: do they align? (mismatch => negotiate SLA and schedule)
Has the customer signed required DPA / data transfer addenda? (no => block until completed for exports involving PII)
Required approvals checklist: Solutions Eng, Security, Legal, PM, and Eng owners (as applicable)
routing_rules: Low risk (no PII, aggregation-only): CS triage -> Solutions Eng resolution within 5 business days
Medium risk (limited PII, time-limited retention change): CS triage -> Solutions Eng + Security review -> Delivery within 10 business days
High risk (raw logs with PII, cross-region exports): CS triage -> Immediate Legal + Security notification -> Eng change or approved export with audit trail; SLA negotiated on case-by-case basis
Export requests that require data extraction from private deployments (VPC/on-prem): route to Customer Success + Enterprise Solutions and include customer runbook for on-prem access
If request involves new product telemetry or schema changes, create child ENG ticket and classify as project work with release timeline
sla_targets: Acknowledgement: <= 1 business day for all requests
Initial risk assessment & routing: <= 2 business days
Decision/Approval for Low risk: <= 5 business days
Decision/Approval for Medium risk: <= 10 business days
Decision/Approval for High risk: SLA negotiated, target 15 business days for initial remediation plan
Delivery/Implementation timelines depend on Eng estimate and release cycles; customer notified within approval window
templates_and_artifacts: GitHub: PR #2894 (solutions-eng/triage-forms) - intake form validation schema
Dashboard: Grafana link for audit export job success/failure metrics: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/data-exports/exports-overview
Email template: email_to_customer_data_exports_v1 (CS use for clarification requests)
implementation_notes: Start with a soft rollout: publish intake template to CS, collect 10 live tickets in pilot over 2 weeks
Automate routing tags in Zendesk using intake form answers to pre-populate triage queue
Add minimal telemetry: create a ‘data_control_request’ event in ingestion pipeline to track lifecycle
For Private/VPC customers, require an ‘on-prem export runbook’ attachment before scheduling work
Eng scope should distinguish between configuration changes (low effort) vs code/telemetry changes (higher effort)
Work with Legal to prepare a fast-track sign-off for routine retention extensions under standard NDA/DPA
examples: Example 1: Customer requests 90-day retention for full request logs to satisfy internal audit. Intake shows no PII, but includes IP addresses. Decision: propose masked export with netflow aggregates; Solutions Eng + Security approve within 5 days

Example 2: Enterprise customer requests bulk audit export including user identifiers for eDiscovery. Intake shows regulatory driver. Decision: escalate to Legal + Security; require DPA addendum and HSM-backed export; delivery plan created and Eng ticket opened
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: ad-hoc exports leak PII -> Mitigation: require owner-level approvals + temporary access tokens + audit trail storage
Risk: SLA creep and increased Eng load -> Mitigation: introduce queued implementation windows and chargeable Professional Services for major exports
Risk: cross-region legal exposure -> Mitigation: block transfers until Legal sign-off and DPA in place
